Engagement parties

The first party after the yes

Usually 40 to 80 guests, planned in three to four months, and the first time most couples organise anything together. It is also the moment your wedding guest list quietly gets decided.

Get party planning quotesParty planning services
  • Long lunches, cocktail parties and backyards
  • Three to four month lead time
  • Free to enquire

Who hosts an engagement party now, and who pays for it?

Most often the couple hosts and pays, sometimes with a contribution from one or both sets of parents. The old convention that the bride's parents host and announce the engagement has largely gone. What replaced it is a conversation.

Have it early and make it specific. Vague offers cause most of the friction, because a parent who would love to contribute and a couple who assume that means the catering are describing different things. Ask for an amount or an item, and confirm it in a message. If one family contributes more, decide what that buys in guest numbers before invitations go out.

Two or three hosts, one decision maker

If parents are involved, agree who has the final call on the guest list and the budget before you book. Split authority turns a happy party into a negotiation.

Say who is paying when you enquire

Planners quote differently when the client and the payer are different people, because it changes who approves what.

The rule

The guest list rule that catches everyone out

Anyone at the engagement party has to be invited to the wedding. Treat it as fixed, because your guests do.

This is the one convention that has survived, and breaking it causes real hurt. If somebody celebrates your engagement, buys a gift and toasts you in front of a room, they will expect a wedding invitation. Leaving them off reads as a demotion.

So the party is where your wedding guest list is actually set, months before you write it. A couple planning a 70 guest wedding who hold a 100 person party has committed to a 100 guest wedding, or to thirty difficult conversations. Draft the wedding list first and build the party inside it.

There is one exception. If the wedding is genuinely tiny, say so on the invitation. Guests accept a small wedding when told at the start.

Work out the wedding number first

Even a rough wedding guest count changes what the party can be. The wedding guide covers how the shape of the day drives that number.

Timing

When should the engagement party actually be?

The usual window is one to four months after the proposal and at least six months before the wedding. Too soon and you are planning a party while still telling people. Too close and the same guests travel, give and take a weekend twice in a season, which is where goodwill thins.

On a long engagement, hold it early. Eighteen months out it feels like a celebration; three weeks out it feels like a rehearsal dinner nobody scheduled.

Three to four months suits almost any format. The exception is a Saturday night at a popular venue in November or December, which competes with every work Christmas party in the country.

Formats

Which format suits the two of you?

Format decides cost, length and how the night feels far more than styling does.

01

A long lunch

Twenty to fifty guests around a shared table. Everybody talks to everybody and it ends while people are still enjoying it. The most reliable format here, and the hardest to scale past fifty.

02

A cocktail party

Sixty to a hundred and twenty guests, standing, canapes and a bar. Best when the two families do not know each other, because standing rooms mix.

03

At home or in a backyard

The most personal and the most work. You control the guest list, music and finish time, and inherit parking, power, weather and the clean up. Hire a bar service, or you will spend your own party pouring drinks.

04

A restaurant or bar function room

A set menu, a minimum spend and almost no planning. You give up styling control and get a whole weekend back.

05

A party at a venue

A hired space with your own caterer, drinks and music. This behaves like a small wedding and most often needs help.

Do you need speeches?

No. An engagement party is the one celebration where speeches are genuinely optional, and a long formal set is the most common complaint guests have. If you want them, keep it to two, cap each at three minutes and do them early.

Checklist

How to plan an engagement party, counting back from the day

An engagement party checklist built for a three to four month lead time. Bring it forward for a Saturday night in November or December.

A working engagement party checklist. Shorten the timings if you must, but keep the order.
WhenWhat to do
Twelve to sixteen weeks outAgree the hosts, the payer and the decision maker. Draft the wedding guest list, then set the party number inside it. Choose the format and budget.
Ten to twelve weeks outBook the venue or confirm the property. If there is a minimum spend, get it in writing now, because it decides everything after.
Eight weeks outBook catering and drinks and decide on a bar service. Send a save the date if guests travel.
Six weeks outSend invitations with a clear finish time. Confirm the music and anything the venue is not providing.
Four weeks outChase guests who have not replied and confirm numbers with catering. Decide on speeches. Sort parking and the wet weather plan.
Two weeks outConfirm every supplier in writing with an arrival time and access point. Write a running order.
The week ofSend the running order to everyone helping. Confirm numbers again and decide who is taking photographs.
On the dayHand the running order to someone who is not you, arrive before the first guest, then stop working.

Scroll the table sideways to see every column.

Working out how to plan an engagement party is mostly this list. If it is more than you want to hold, on-the-day coordination covers the last two rows.

Ideas

Engagement party ideas, grouped by what you want to spend

Good engagement party ideas are about format and setting rather than decoration. These are grouped by budget.

Low key, low cost

A backyard barbecue with a keg and a shared playlist. A picnic in a park with a permit. A Sunday lunch where everyone pays for their own meal, which is fine if the invitation says so.

Middle of the road

A function room with a grazing table and a capped bar tab. A pub garden booked for an afternoon. A boat charter split across a group. Or a cocktail party at home with a mobile bar.

Going bigger

A dry hire warehouse or gallery with your own caterer and a band, or a winery lunch with transport laid on. At this level you are running a small event, which is where couples first bring in help.

Party planners

Engagement party ideas that cost nothing

Put the two families at one table rather than opposite ends of the room. Print six photographs and put them where people queue. Set a finish time on the invitation.

Engagement party ideas worth skipping

A three hour speech list. A cash bar at a party you called a celebration. A theme that makes guests buy something. And a guest list padded with people you feel you should invite.

If the party doubles as the reveal

Some couples fold the party into a proposal reveal, with friends waiting somewhere the person does not know about. It works, but the proposal happens privately first.

Straight answers

Engagement party questions

Do you have to invite engagement party guests to the wedding?

Yes. Treat it as fixed. Anyone who celebrates your engagement, brings a gift and toasts you will expect a wedding invitation. The only exception is a genuinely tiny wedding, and you have to say so on the invitation.

Who pays for an engagement party?

Most often the couple, frequently with a contribution from one or both sets of parents. The old rule about the bride's family hosting has largely gone. What matters is that a contribution is agreed as a specific amount or item before you book.

How long before the wedding should the engagement party be?

One to four months after the proposal, and at least six months before the wedding. Holding it close asks the same guests to travel and give twice in a short run.

Do we need speeches at an engagement party?

No, and plenty of good parties have none. If you want them, keep it to two speakers, three minutes each, early in the night. Tell them the limit, because the most common guest complaint is a speech list that ran half an hour.

Do I need an engagement party planner, or can we do it ourselves?

Most couples run a 40 to 80 guest party themselves, particularly at a restaurant handling food and drink. Help is worth buying for a dry hire space, or a party at home. An engagement party planner can be engaged for the day only, and most will bring engagement party ideas from events they have already run.

One enquiry, then it is somebody else's job

Tell us about the engagement party

The rough date, the area, the guest count, and whether you want help planning it or just running it.
